text: Got it — I replayed to this frame: your last popcorn kill was about two seconds before you flagged, and the two turrets are still crawling in above the top edge, so there was nothing to shoot for roughly two to three seconds. Noted the positive too — the music kicking in when the turrets land. One question: while you were waiting for the next wave, what were you doing with the ship?

Replayed it. You had speed-killed everything in the alley's first pass — all four turrets and every popcorn — then a bullet got you mid-screen a moment before you flagged. Logging both of your points: the grey shapes of similar size, and the top-side entry not feeling right. One question: just before you died there, what did you think shot you?

Thank you — and good catch. That one's a bug on my side, not a design question: the sprite's nose followed the popcorn's stored speed, but their real flight adds a side-to-side wobble bigger than that speed, so the nose lagged the actual direction. Fixed in the renderer; it takes effect when you next refresh the Booth (that restarts the run, so finish this one first if you like). Keep going.

Not intentional — it's a bug, and thank you for flagging it instead of assuming it was on purpose. The midboss's side-to-side sweep runs off a clock that started when it spawned, so the moment it finishes floating down the sweep is already most of the way to a rail and it snaps there. I'm fixing it so the sweep begins from the centre where it parks. Nothing for you to answer here; keep going.

Logged — the stage track carrying on under the WARNING and the boss music. Sounds like a bug in the handoff between the two tracks rather than a design choice; I'm checking the audio code now and will fix it if it's what I think. Keep playing.

On the music: the code says the stage track should fade to silence during the WARNING and the boss track should take over. To pin it down — when the boss music starts, do you hear BOTH tracks at once, or does the stage track keep going with NO boss music underneath?

That settles it — the boss handoff is fine; the WARNING was only fading the stage track out over about a second, so it was still audible under the siren. Changed it to a hard cut, the way arcade warnings do it. Takes effect on your next refresh. Thanks — that's three real bugs from one session.

You read it exactly right, and the code agrees: the real hit point is a 3px circle at the ship's origin — which is the TOP point of that purple triangle, not its middle — and it was only drawn while focusing. Fixed: the purple is now a small canopy centred on the true core, and the core dot is always visible (focus adds a ring around it). Bullets also have their own 3px radius, so 'edge of the dot touching the edge of the bullet' is a hit — that's the honest rule to learn. Takes effect on refresh. Player and boss redesign proper: logging as the next art items.
Logged: boss art to match the new families — three forms already, but they're still plain geometry. That's the next art pass after the player. Nothing to answer; keep going.

Checked the research and the code: you're right about the principle, and the numbers explain the feel. The hit circle is only 3px (Cave-small) — but bullets carry their own 3px, so a bullet kills when its centre is within 6px of the dot, and the ship was just 18px wide. That's a 3:1 ship-to-hitbox ratio; Cave ships run 8–10:1. So the fix is the ship, not the hitbox: it's now a 28px delta with the canopy centred on the core, the core dot always visible, and the focus ring is gone (it was reading as 'half the ship'). Refresh to see it; the gallery page shows a bullet at the true kill distance next to the focused ship.
